title: Juniper and the Rivergate
premise: Astrid Oyelaran, a desert ranger chasing a thief who stole nothing but a name, crosses paths with a dying prospector named Juniper Hale, who trades him a map to the Rivergate — a legendary water source buried beneath the salt flats — in exchange for a promise: deliver it to his estranged daughter, Wren. Astrid and Wren assemble a ragtag expedition of debtors and drifters, only to discover the Rivergate is real, guarded by the descendants of the town that drowned to hide it, and coveted by the magistrate who ruined Juniper's life. When the gate is opened, it reveals not treasure but the truth of a massacre the town's founders committed, and Astrid must choose between the loyalty he owes his crew and the truth Wren deserves about her father's role in the cover-up. In the end, they flood the archive of lies, release the water to the drought-stricken lowlands, and return home as a family bound not by blood or promise, but by what they chose to tell.
about_author: Emrys Eriksen is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent six years mapping dry riverbeds across three continents before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who inherit more than they asked for.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Stole Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. Ranger Astrid Oyelaran tracks a thief across the empty flats for nine days, only to find the man stole nothing but a dead prospector's name from a registry office. The absurdity gnaws at him; he can't close the case on a stolen name. Emotional beat: restless obsession disguised as duty.

chapters.title: A Compass and a Debt
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. Broke and off-contract, Astrid stops at a waystation where the dying prospector Juniper Hale recognizes the thief's description. Juniper offers Astrid a map to the Rivergate in exchange for one promise: carry it to his daughter Wren in Saltmere and say nothing else. Emotional beat: a bargain struck too fast to regret.

chapters.title: Saltmere
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. Saltmere is a company town dying of thirst and magistrates' taxes. Astrid finds Wren Hale working the desalination pumps, hands scarred, eyes harder than her father described. She refuses the map; her father abandoned her twenty years ago. Emotional beat: grief wearing anger as armor.

chapters.title: The Map That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren studies the map that night and finds her own childhood handwriting in its margins — she helped her father draw it before he left. The realization cracks her refusal open. Emotional beat: betrayal complicated by evidence of love.

chapters.title: Crew of Debtors
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. To cross the flats legally, they need an expedition charter, so Astrid recruits a crew of people with nothing to lose: an ex-magistrate's clerk named Odile, a well-diver called Brannic, and the very thief Astrid was chasing, Tam Voss, who claims he stole the name to save someone. Emotional beat: wary camaraderie forming out of desperation.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Interest
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile recognizes the map's survey marks as sealed government records — the Rivergate appears in documents she once filed and was ordered to forget. Magistrate Corvane summons her; she lies to his face for the first time in her career. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of choosing a side.

chapters.title: Out Past the Markers
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. The expedition leaves Saltmere ahead of Corvane's riders. The flats test them: a whiteout dust storm, Brannic's collapsed well-sense, Tam saving Wren from a sink crust. Trust begins replacing suspicion. Emotional beat: the desert stripping everyone down to essentials.

chapters.title: Juniper's Letters
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Camping in Juniper's old claim shack, Wren finds letters he never sent — twenty years of them, each explaining why he left: he witnessed something at the Rivergate and ran to keep Wren from being silenced too. Emotional beat: forgiveness arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: Riders on the Horizon
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Corvane's riders catch their trail. Tam admits he was originally hired by Corvane to recover the map, then went rogue when he learned what Corvane intended. The crew must decide whether to trust him; Astrid vouches with his ranger's oath. Emotional beat: loyalty tested before it's earned.

chapters.title: The Drowned Town
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. They reach a valley that maps call empty and find ruins beneath the salt — a whole town, flooded and preserved, its wells capped with government seals. Someone didn't just hide the Rivergate; they buried a community. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Keepers
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Descendants of the drowned town emerge — the Keepers — led by an old woman, Sefa, who tests them with questions about Juniper. He was here; he saw the cisterns and the records vault beneath. Sefa offers passage if they swear to tell no one what's below. Emotional beat: hospitality edged with threat.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: POV Brannic. The well-diver leads them down through the town's flooded underlevels to the vault door. Brannic, who has spent his life finding water, feels the pressure of the Rivergate like a heartbeat through stone. Emotional beat: reverence, the closest thing to religion he knows.

chapters.title: What the Vault Holds
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Inside: not gold, but the town's complete records — including proof that Magistrate Corvane's predecessors diverted the river deliberately, drowning the town to monopolize water rights, and that Juniper found the proof and fled rather than be killed for it. Emotional beat: history as a wound still bleeding.

chapters.title: Corvane Arrives
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. Corvane's riders breach the valley with warrants and guns, having tracked them since Saltmere. He offers each crew member amnesty for the map and silence. One by one, they refuse — even Tam, who owes him everything. Emotional beat: solidarity crystallizing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Gate
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The Keepers seal the vault; Corvane lays siege to the ruins, cutting off their water cache. Days grind past. Wren realizes her father didn't run from cowardice — he ran to lead pursuers away from Sefa's people, and never stopped paying for it. Emotional beat: love reassembled from broken pieces.

chapters.title: Tam's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Tam. To buy time, Tam pretends to defect, feeding Corvane false information about the vault's contents. The ruse works until Corvane's clerk recognizes the forgery. Tam is captured and scheduled for execution at dawn. Emotional beat: guilt finally paid down with skin.

chapters.title: The Choice of Waters
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. Astrid discovers the gate mechanism doesn't just open the vault — it releases the river itself, which would flood the lowlands Corvane's patrons farm and destroy the monopoly, but also drown the ruins and everything in them. Opening it means destroying the proof and the past alike. Emotional beat: the weight of a decision no one should carry alone.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The crew splits: some want to preserve the records and expose Corvane legally; others want the water released now, for the dying towns. Wren must decide what her father would have wanted — and realizes he left the choice deliberately unfinished, trusting whoever came after. Emotional beat: inheriting a question instead of an answer.

chapters.title: Dawn Execution
chapters.summary: POV Tam. At dawn, Astrid and Sefa's Keepers stage a diversionary strike on Corvane's camp while Odile forges release orders. Tam walks free, but the escape costs them the element of surprise — Corvane now storms the gate itself. Emotional beat: rescue shadowed by escalation.

chapters.title: Opening the Rivergate
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. Corvane breaches the vault to seize the records for himself. In the confrontation, Astrid turns the gate wheel — not to destroy the truth, but because Wren has already copied the essential pages. Water thunders loose; Corvane's monopoly drowns in the flood along with his men's advance camp. Emotional beat: catharsis at terrible cost.

chapters.title: What We Carried Home
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The expedition returns to Saltmere ahead of the water, delivering both the river and the copied testimony. Corvane is arrested by his own clerks, armed with Odile's evidence. Wren reads her father's final letter aloud at the pump-house; the town listens. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into public memory.

chapters.title: The Promise Kept
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. Months later, the lowlands are green, the case of the stolen name is closed — Tam took it to give a dead friend an identity, and Astrid lets that theft stand. Wren asks Astrid to stay; he unpacks the compass he'd been carrying to pay a debt and gives it to her instead. Emotional beat: a found family, home at last.
